items.body: August 14th was another joyous evening in New Brunswick, New Jersey, which is quickly establishing itself as a hot spot for any touring noise acts to stop through on the east coast. Considering the enthusiastic attendees and diverse local talent pool available for these shows though, this comes off as no surprise. As a result, acts of both the new and old guard are able to use this intimate basement setting as a proving ground to show their stuff to a rather open-minded but critically thinking crowd. So when Midwest noisecore legends Penis Geyser announced they would be touring in celebration of their twentieth anniversary, booking them a show in Hub City was a no-brainer. First act of the night was FRICKER, who I would put into contention as modern noise’s best kept secret anywhere. The unique blend of digital soundscape smashing and crude feedback that he brings to the table can be tailored to just about any sound system that he comes across, which leads to each live experience being different from the last. Given the grimy nature of Ferren Mall’s sound system, I figured the crowd would be in for something on the crustier side of his material. Indeed, I was right on that front. Fricker spared no room for intricacies, and immediately summoned churning rumble grumble to suck the audience into a vacuum of unforgiving sound. The feedback drone that started the set eventually gave way to more variety in the chopping of digital samples, but never once lost its harsh backing. It seems like there is not a single sound system that this red-headed prince can’t conquer, and the audience seemed to think so, as much feedback I heard after was that this set made the travel and admission price alone feel worth it. With a bar set that high, things could only go up from there. When it comes to performances I take part in, I try to often gauge how the audience is feeling about things both during and after the set. With EVIL BONG, this task is never really that hard. Being showered in a sea of audience laughter and “fuck you” cries gives you a good idea of where your performance stands. With 6 members to this unit, every full band blast came closer to sounding like harsh noise wall than perhaps a noisecore band would sound. Between takes, microphone feedback would shriek like a drunken sailor beginning to hurl as song titles that took shots at New Brunswick, the audience, the bands playing and more came out of the mouth of their jackass drummer (side note: that guy really is a jerk). By the end of the set, with the audience in a frenzy, several members of the band just began to throw themselves directly at the audience. Hey, if hurting them emotionally won’t break their spirits, why not try physically?? By the time the band finished their crowd-pleasing closer, “Fuck Scronch,” there was simply nothing more they could do than to cheer and submit to the power of Evil Bong. Much like the film series this band was named after, audiences can’t help but find entertainment in the horror of this performance. To simply shower praise towards PENIS GEYSER would not be enough to describe the masterclass their performance was. While most seasoned attendees of noise shows expect short sets, nobody was expecting just 90 seconds from this touring unit. It’s 20 years of the band, you would be more than understanding if they wanted to play a long set. Nope; 90 seconds and it’s off the stage. But in that time, the band managed to whip the audience between blasting frenzy, tense restraint and dadaist rock n roll deconstruction that would have left the most seasoned of touring acts in absolute disbelief by how disciplined the trio were in their attack. While the blasting noisecore is what most of us came for, I found myself more intrigued by the moments in between, when drummer Mikeal VanCleave would gently tap on his kit while the string slinging duo of Brad Griggs and Charlie Mumma would treat their guitars as anything other than traditional songwriting. Strings were detuned, slapped around, beaten and mangled. The frenetic energy of these actions sounded closer to someone rattling their cabinet around than actually attempting to play anything musical. And when it all finally came to an end, it wasn’t bombastic. The band simply stopped playing whatever interlude they were in the midst of and started breaking their gear down. The audience cheered for an encore. I heard “One more! One more!” cried out repeatedly (what would even be “one more” for this band? Certainly not a song). Finally, one attendee walking out said “nah, it was perfect” and left. I couldn’t have said it better myself; a phenomenal band that could go on for another 20 years and probably still be as good. The new blood of New Jersey closed the evening’s happenings, as SPLOOGE RECEPTACLE came out with a table full of gear and the enthusiasm to inject their own brand of reckless abandon onto the audience. For those maybe not in the know, this group serves as the house band for New Jersey–based record label, NJMA, which has taken on the mantle of all things absurd and limited-edition in the Garden State. There are too many projects and releases to even begin listing the “essentials,” but Splooge Receptacle is where all these insane minds come together to celebrate the power of all things noise and core. Members were switching between duties on the mic, guitar, drums, electronics, etc. Really, if someone felt like they wanted to play something more than another member at the moment, they made the switch off occur. Similar to the Evil Bong performance from earlier, Splooge also engaged in their own form of audience antagonizing, as members crashed into the crowd while raging out through the wall of sound. Even when sound was not always perfect (sorry for providing a bad cable, team), their reckless abandon carried the set a great deal. With each passing set this group does, I become more and more excited at the prospect of where their sound can go. This group will be a name to look out for in the coming years if your listening diet tends to lean towards the more lo-fi ends of noisecore and shitnoise. So with the final blastbeat sounding off, the crowd took the streets, wandering off to who-the-hell-knows until the next show. Maybe some went to the nearest eatery available. Personally speaking, I went off to the Edison Diner for some late-night nachos with the Penis Geyser crew in tow. But maybe some walked away from this one thinking of how inspiring it could be to see the most chaotic and shittiest sounds performed so excellently. I know plenty that are still buzzing days later from the whole affair.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评记录了新泽西州新布朗斯维克一场地下噪音拼盘演出。首位登场的FRICKER以数字采样碎裂与粗糙反馈为核心，在演出场地简陋的音响系统上构建出令人窒息的低频漩涡，每场演出因设备不同而呈现独特面貌。第二组EVIL BONG作为六人编制乐队，其全面爆发的音响墙已逼近harsh noise wall的质感，演出过程中夹杂着对城市、乐迷及其他乐队的恶意攻击性喊话，主唱兼鼓手以挑衅姿态著称，结尾曲《Fuck Scronch》将现场推向高潮。整体氛围粗粝、攻击性强，强调现场体验的不可复制性，反映了美国东海岸地下噪音场景的活力与多样性。

items.body: The Greek duo Incirrina, George Katsanos and Irini Tiniakou, formed in Athens in late 2017. On May 29, 2026 they released their third album, “Trace”, through the German label Cold Transmission Music on vinyl, CD, limited cassette and digital. Across three albums the pair have moved from darkwave towards minimal and electro-wave, built on analogue synthesizers, drum machines and Tiniakou’s vocals. I spoke to both of them about the record, the poet who writes their lyrics and what a two-person setup can carry onstage. (Courtesy by Inferno Sound Diaries) Trace by Incirrina Incirrina interview Q: “Trace” is already your third full-length album. Looking back on everything you’ve achieved so far, how do you view your journey as a band? And how would you describe and introduce this new record to people who may not have heard it yet? George: Indeed, after the releases of the albums “8.15” (2019) and “Lip Led Scream” (2022), we are happy to have our third LP “Trace” out by the label Cold Transmission, released 29.5.2026. We consider the band as a space for exploration, experimentation, personal expression, also as an inner journey and diving into our souls. Incirrina has brought us the joy of sharing our music with people across multiple countries. Until now we have toured in 12 European countries and played in many gigs and festivals, which led to beautiful and completely new experiences. Irini: In this album, we experimented with instrumentation, rhythm and vocal approach. We used a combination of analogue synthesizers, drum machines, octapad, electric bass guitar, electric piano and acoustic instruments such as kantele, waterphone, melodica. “Trace” includes 11 songs written between 2023-2025 in a 24-channel console, that belong in the genres of dark electronic, synth-wave and cold-wave. The minimal-synth and post-punk roots of our previous albums are still obvious, yet the new songs are enriched with dynamism, depth, and rhythmic diversity and we also explored new ways of delivering the vocals for this album. Also we would like to note that this album is the result of the collaboration of many people who put their heart and talent into it, and we are grateful to them – these people are Dimitris Dimitriadis (mixing), Anestis Psaradakos (mastering), uBuDancer (artwork, analogue collage), Nestor Theophilopoulos (photography), Maria Deligiorgi/Infrared Media (layout) and Suzy Hermann and Andreas Hermann of Cold Transmission. Q: If I’m not mistaken, you’ve been active for almost ten years now. How did Incirrina come into being, and how have both your collaboration and the band itself evolved over the years? George: Our common journey as Incirrina started in late 2017. Since both of us are professional musicians and music teachers, we’ve been involved in numerous bands and projects and music has always been the center of our lives, but neither of us had ever been in a purely synth band before. It was a great pleasure to discover already in our first meeting, in September 2014, that we had the exact same taste in music – we were talking for hours about Jean Michel Jarre, Joy Division, The Cure, Kraftwerk and numerous others… We became a couple, still the timing for forming a band wasn’t right yet – we were working hard in teaching and the other projects, and simply didn’t have the time to start something new together. But in 2017 life brought things together in such a way that conditions were created for something new to be born. Incirrina came into life with the aim to make music in the style we’ve deeply loved since we were teenagers. Irini: The first tracks were written right in our living room. Although I do write lyrics, we chose to base our songs on the poetry of William Blake, an artist we both deeply adore. After recording 6 songs, and without thinking twice, we uploaded them on Bandcamp (this was the first EP “8.15”, in December 2018), and suddenly something clicked. We received an unexpected wave of enthusiasm from complete strangers. Essentially, we started with no expectations other than making songs that we liked. It was magical how this evolved. One year later, in late 2019, the Greek label Geheimnis Records released “8.15” as an LP – the first 6 songs plus 5 new ones. Then COVID hit. During those strange years of isolation, we wrote the songs for our second album, “Lip Led Scream”, which was released by Cold Transmission in August 2022. One thing naturally led to another; some months before the lockdown, we had received an invitation to perform in Germany, in Slow Club Freiburg, a show that finally came to life in May 2022. That was the spark that started this beautiful adventure of European tours and live shows. In the years leading up to this year’s release of “Trace”, we focused on live performances as well as exploring new sounds and we also scored two theatrical plays in Athens. We are quite strict with our music, even though we compose new tracks very quickly, the ones we choose to release are very few (for every track we release, about four or five others are left behind). George: We really enjoy jamming and playing together, most of our tracks come alive through this very process. But there are also songs written entirely by one of us, then the other one enriched or reshaped them, regarding arrangement or structure. While we co-write the harmonic and melodic elements of our songs and handle the arrangements together, our individual roles are quite distinct. I focus on the rhythmic side, taking care of the live drums and drum programming, also the basslines and the riffs, while Irini handles the vocals. Q: One of the defining characteristics of your music is your use of analogue synthesizers. That seems like a very deliberate choice. What is it about analogue synths that continues to inspire you, and how has this aspect of your sound evolved over the years, particularly on “Trace”? George: Indeed, we have a great love for analog sound and analog synthesizers. Of course, there are plenty digital instruments we really like and also use. I adore Moog synthesizers, their rich harmonic sound fills the ear with very distinct frequencies. I love that you can never have the exact same sound. The instruments that I use do not have a “preset” or “save” possibility, so every time I make the sound from the beginning and I find this really thrilling. Analog synthesizers have personality; I feel like I’m using a sonic canvas when playing them, their sound has so many shades and details. Irini: We’ve used analog synths on all of our albums. In “Trace”, we paired them with acoustic instruments and also some digital synths, like the AKAI MPC and the Yamaha PS-55. Even though the Yamaha is digital, it’s from way back in 1983, and its sound has this nostalgic warmth that really speaks to us. Our relationship with instruments is just like with people… we have great chemistry and love for some, while others we just can’t connect with at all! An instrument is a whole world of its own, and a single sound can inspire an entire song. Some tracks started out just from a single sound, like the song “She Is In The Dream”. We also love building lots of layers and textures when it comes to orchestration, and our analog synths are perfect for mixing and layering in different ways. Q: Are you essentially a duo or more of a trio? I ask because I noticed that your lyrics are not always written by the two of you. Could you explain how that collaboration works, and how the lyrical themes develop in relation to your own musical ideas? Irini: Musically speaking, we’re definitely a duo; the two of us write and play all the music, and we handle everything that goes into running a band. But at the same time we also have a “secret” third member. This is the poet Konstantinos Londos, whom we are lucky enough to have in our lives as a very special and dearly loved friend. He wrote the lyrics for our last two albums (with the exception of two songs, one on each record). Konstantinos puts what we feel and want to communicate into words in the most wonderful way. Working with him is magical. A lot of times we’ll discuss a topic that’s really on our minds, and then Konstantinos will write a poem about it… and just like that, we have the lyrics for a song. Other times, we picked some of his existing poems that spoke to our hearts, set them to music, and turned them into songs (like “Mutate” and “Alien Room”). But either way, there’s always an incredible creative process between the 3 of us – we listen together to the musical ideas, discuss the meaning of the lyrics, how the words flow melodically, and their deeper impact. In the end, after plenty of changes and fine-tuning (and sometimes after a lot of tears) the song finally takes its true shape. Konstantinos has a rare gift for clarity, simplicity, humor, sensitivity and working together with him is really a pleasure. He is an explosive mix of a brilliant Renaissance man, a Homo Universalis, and someone who genuinely prefers to stay out of the spotlight. Q: Speaking of the lyrics, “Trace” is an intriguing title that can be interpreted in many different ways. The album also explores profound and, at times, rather introspective themes. Could you tell us more about the concept behind the album? And to what extent do the lyrics shape the atmosphere of the music, or is it sometimes the other way around? Irini: Finding the right album title is usually a tricky process, since it needs to capture a lot of different concepts in just a few words. But with “Trace”, things were easier – the title came about completely spontaneously from Konstantinos, right after a chat about what making this album meant to us. The word means “imprint”, and that’s exactly what this record is: the footprint of a collaboration between people trying to capture in sounds and words the things that spark their thoughts and haunt their nights. This is also stated in the album’s back cover: “Trace” is the imprint of “searching for wondrous, meaningful diversions, novel transformations and transitory acts of care and defiance”. Thematically the songs deal with the uniqueness of human experience and the struggle of not losing one’s inner freedom and individuality in dystopian times – the “seeming real” where all that is imposed and inhumane presents itself as the inevitable truth (“Always Here”). Celebrating diversity and self-expression, but always connecting and creating with other people, is a way out (“Mutate”). And the album itself is the result of such a process; we consider ourselves, against the odds, as artisans and friends who make music, share it and reinvent ourselves. Other songs cover universal, age-old themes like love, loneliness, the fear of loss, pain of death (“Sometimes”, “Region”), also the relationship with oneself and the connection with the world outside (“Diver”, “Find”), themes like the dream element, the urban landscape, and mysterious, fairy-like figures are touched upon in the songs “Alexia”, “Presence”, “She Is In The Dream”; burning issues of our time like domestic violence (“Alien Room”); and how the “self” connects with today’s world, showing endless introspection but a lack of empathy, human pain, and the way we try to hide it even from ourselves (“ΚΡΥΦΟ”, which means “Hidden”, the only track in Greek language). George: Since songwriting is a two-way street, as we described earlier, the atmosphere that is created depends on each individual song. When we start composing music for an existing poem, we are influenced by the content, the meaning of the lyrics, and the rhythm of the words and syllables. Conversely, Konstantinos would often listen to a musical theme we had composed and write lyrics over it, based on a topic that was on our minds and that we had been discussing. However, since the general vibe of our music and lyrics is already introspective and relatively dark, we take it for granted that we won’t stray from that… not out of principle, but because the darker element simply speaks to us emotionally and temperamentally. Q: How do you approach your live performances? More specifically, how do you translate the layered studio recordings, and especially the analogue elements, to the stage? George: Being a duo has a lot of advantages, like flexibility with rehearsals, the creative process, and traveling. But also has plenty of challenges… Practically speaking, if we wanted to perform our tracks live with their full studio orchestration, we would definitely need at least one more musician on stage. Our compromise is to use backing tracks for the drums, or a portion of them while I play the rest, and then we perform the melodic and bass lines live. We inevitably have to skip several elements from the album… still that’s not necessarily a bad thing for a live performance, because different things take priority on stage. Also, for gigs, we bring along smaller gear. It would be practically impossible for just two people to travel carrying the actual instruments we used to compose and record, so we adapt our sound to smaller, more flexible instruments, which are a mix of analog, hybrid, and digital instruments. When we play in our hometown, things are much easier and we can bring along some of the original (and heavy) instruments used in the recording. But when it comes to touring abroad, since we travel by plane and train, doing that would totally be out of the question for practical reasons. Irini: Over time, we’ve rearranged some tracks for our live shows to such an extent that they end up sounding quite different from the studio recordings, in terms of orchestration, tempo, and also vocals. This is especially true for songs from our first album. Also, since we love improvisation, we play the tracks a bit differently at almost every gig. We add intros, change up some riffs, and basically transform them depending on the mood of the moment. It would be really interesting at some point to make an album with our older songs exactly as they are played live, in a live recording setup. This happened already with one song, the “Only One Smile Alone”; the original one is “The Smile”, and following the suggestion of Andreas Hermann, we recorded it again in the way we play it live. Q: Finally, with an album title like “Trace”, it seems only natural to ask: what kind of trace do you hope this album, and Incirrina’s music in general, will leave behind? And what lies ahead for the band in the coming months? Irini: What we truly want with all our hearts is this: for people who will listen to our music, to feel something, to be moved, to dance, to feel good, or to find a personal meaning in our songs. Through our music, we aren’t seeking self-expression as much as we are seeking connection and co-motion, sharing in something as beautiful as music. We would love for the music of Incirrina to leave a small imprint of beauty in this world. Everything is fleeting and surely everything fades into the oblivion of time, but we would be incredibly happy if, even for just a few moments, we could bring joy to some people… just as we experience the joy of making songs and playing together, in rehearsals or in live shows. George: In the coming months, we will mainly focus on presenting “Trace” through live performances in Greece and Europe. We definitely want to work on producing some new songs as well, and we also plan to celebrate our 10th anniversary as a band with something special, which we will announce in early 2027…! Thank you for this interview, and we wish all the very best to you and your readers! Incirrina About Incirrina Incirrina is a dark electronic and minimal synth duo based in Athens, Greece, formed in late 2017 by George Katsanos (analogue synthesizers, octapad, drum programming, electric bass guitar, kantele, alto melodica, waterphone, samples, vocals) and Irini Tiniakou (synthesizers, vocals). The pair had met in September 2014 and were already working as musicians and music teachers in other projects before Incirrina became one of their own. Tiniakou first appeared as a guest vocalist on a release by the Greek act Metal Disco before the duo started releasing under their own name. Their first six songs, built on the poetry of William Blake, went up on Bandcamp as the EP “8.15” in December 2018. The Greek label Geheimnis Records issued “8.15” as an LP in late 2019, adding five new tracks to the original six. The digital maxi-single “Utter” followed in 2020, and in 2021 the duo shared a split maxi-single with The Man & His Failures, “Devastations / R.Daneel”, on Smash Records. Their second album, “Lip Led Scream”, arrived in August 2022 and was their first record for Germany’s Cold Transmission Music, which has handled their releases since. Reviewing it for Side-Line in 2023, Inferno Sound Diaries described it as “a pure Cold-Wave production which is sometimes reinforced with harder, EBM, elements” and “a well-crafted and fully enjoyable work without any single cut to throw away”. In September 2024 the duo returned with the double single “Immersion”, pairing “Presence” and “Alien Room”, again on Cold Transmission Music. Incirrina have performed in twelve European countries, including Greece, Germany, Belgium, Hungary and Croatia, with appearances at Plíísken Festival, Morphic Festival, Cold Transmission Festival, Death Disco Festival – The Warm Up, Athens Music Week, Metavasis Festival and the Athens Digital Arts Festival. Their live show began with an invitation to Slow Club Freiburg, a booking made before the pandemic that finally took place in May 2022. In the years between “Lip Led Scream” and “Trace” they also scored two theatrical plays in Athens. “Trace”, the duo’s third album, was released on May 29, 2026 on Cold Transmission Music across black and crystal-clear vinyl, CD, a limited cassette and digital. Its eleven tracks were written between 2023 and 2025 and recorded through a 24-channel console. Lyrics are by the poet Konstantinos Londos, except “Sometimes”, written by Incirrina. Dimitris Dimitriadis mixed the album and Anestis Psaradakos mastered it, with artwork by uBuDancer, photography by Nestor Theophilopoulos and layout by Maria Deligiorgi/Infrared Media. “Mutate” and “Always Here” preceded the album as singles, and “Mutate” was issued with a video. Side-Line’s review of “Trace” rated it 8/10. The duo say the next months go to live shows in Greece and Europe, with a tenth-anniversary announcement planned for early 2027.
items._cn_summary: 希腊二人组合 Incirrina 由 George Katsanos 与 Irini Tiniakou 组成，2017年末在雅典成立。2026年5月通过德国厂牌 Cold Transmission Music 发行第三张专辑《Trace》，包含11首2023至2025年间创作的作品。专辑以模拟合成器、鼓机、octapad、电贝斯、电钢琴为核心，并引入康特勒琴、水琴、 melodica 等原声乐器，丰富了此前以极简合成器与后朋克为底色的声响。在人声处理上亦进行了新的探索，使作品在动力学、层次感与节奏多样性上有所推进。混音、母带及封面设计分别由 Dimitris Dimitriadis、Anestis Psaradakos 及 uBuDancer 等合作者完成。乐队迄今已在12个欧洲国家巡演，将组合视为探索、实验与内心旅程的空间。

items.body: Brian Stillman is an American artist based in New York who is releasing his debut album, “Terminal Days”, featuring nine tracks. The album is politically engaged, with a raised middle finger directed at fascists, oligarchs, tech bros, A.I. fetishists, and human rights abusers. The music sounds like pure, good old-fashioned Industrial-Metal. The guitar riffs leave no doubt about it, backed by hellish rhythms and vocals loaded with rage. Despite the sheer power of this Industrial-Metal assault, there are also a few more refined Pop arrangements to be found. This makes the whole thing highly accessible, but believe me, the album remains packed with adrenaline from start to finish. There is a fine balance between the guitar work and the synths, creating a powerful and dynamic sound. Ministry fans will undoubtedly appreciate this project. “Terminal Days” sounds like a very promising debut album, and Negative Agent is undoubtedly a name to keep in mind. (Rating:7)-. Listen to “Annihilation Kick”: Annihilation Kick by Negative Agent About Negative Agent Negative Agent is the solo industrial-metal project of American musician Brian Stillman, who is based in New York. Stillman writes all music and lyrics and handles guitars, synth and percussion programming, sampling and vocals. The debut album “Terminal Days” was self-released on 8 April 2026 in digital, CD and cassette formats. Steve Wiener plays a guest guitar solo on “Mind Wipe” and Greg Schwan plays guest bass on “Pain Control”. The record also carries a bonus remix of “Fascist Beatdown” by Voidscan. Stillman mixed the album and designed the cover art; Hillary Johnson mastered it at Kale Shelter Studios. On the Bandcamp page for the release, Stillman states that “Negative Agent is 100% Human. No A.I. is used in any capacity, ever.” “Terminal Days” is the project’s first full-length and its first entry in the Side-Line archive.
items._cn_summary: Brian Stillman的首张专辑《Terminal Days》以九首曲目构建了一种纯粹且带有强烈政治立场的工业金属表达，歌词明确指向法西斯主义者、寡头、科技精英与人工智能崇拜者等社会议题。吉他riff构成作品骨架，配合地狱般的节奏与充满愤怒的嗓音，形成持续的高强度冲击。同时，制作中融入了若干精致的流行编曲元素，提升了可听性，但并未削弱整体的肾上腺素感。吉他与合成器之间维持着良好平衡，塑造出强劲而动态的声响。客座吉他与贝斯出现在特定曲目中，另有Fascist Beatdown的Voidscan混音版作为附赠。作者强调百分之百人类创作，不使用任何人工智能。这是Side-Line档案中该项目首次正式收录。

items.body: By the time Syna Awel reaches “Incantation”, the sun has dropped. It closes an open-air acoustic session she filmed in a single afternoon this year, five Amazigh songs in a row, the last easing into a jam as the daylight goes. She is Franco-Algerian, a singer and percussionist who grew up in Aït Bouaddou, a village in the Kabyle mountains of northern Algeria. Her songs come out of Amazigh oral tradition, poetry and melody carried by voice, and she brings them into contemporary jazz. For the session she sings with Luc Lavenne on guitar, Anis Agrebi on oud, Tony Sgro on derbouka and Mahir Bostandzija on percussion. Where the album set her voice against jazz piano and bendir, this acoustic line-up answers with oud and hand percussion. Awel sings “Incantation” in Kabyle. The line “Kul yiwen yesɛa tidet-ines” means everyone holds their own truth, and the next line adds that everyone does what they can. She sets that against the turning of a day: the sun sets, the moon takes the evening, and it all comes round again. The songs come from Awel, her 2024 debut, arranged by drummer Karim Ziad and released on Imago Records. The full session, subtitled in Kabyle and French, plays on her YouTube channel. Stream “Incantation” HERE and get your copy of Awel following THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Syna Awel – Incantation (Acoustic Live Session) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: Syna Awel 是一位法裔阿尔及利亚歌手与打击乐手，成长于卡比利亚山区村庄。她的创作根植于阿马齐格口头传统，以诗歌与声乐旋律为载体，将北非民间音乐带入当代爵士语境。这张原声现场录制于一个下午，五首阿马齐格歌曲依次展开，伴随日落光线渐暗自然过渡到即兴段落。与原专辑的爵士钢琴与本迪尔鼓配置不同，现场改用乌德琴与手鼓，呼应传统质感。歌词以卡比尔语演唱，探讨每个人持有自身真理的主题，歌词意象与昼夜轮转相交织。专辑由鼓手 Karim Ziad 编排，发行于独立厂牌 Imago Records。其音乐将地方口头传统与爵士即兴结构相融合，展现了北非原声音乐与现代音乐语言之间的对话可能。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目以传统音乐为底色，融入每位乐手的个人视角。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗粝的奔跑节奏展示主唱富有说服力的嗓音；唯一原创曲目《Nordgård》由成员Morten Musicus创作，口琴与风笛带来强劲推进力。传统曲《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》以洋琴为细腻背景，收尾曲《Orms》作为器乐曲将口簧琴、长笛与弦乐混合，营造出令人兴奋的失衡感。整体呈现出古老、吱嘎作响的氛围，乐队展现出超出其新身份的成熟度与完成度。五首曲目虽短，却是一次强有力的开端。

items.excerpt:

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / sound documentary / freestyle rap
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述实录。二十五位年龄从十七岁到六十七岁的参与者分享了他们的亲身经历，部分内容即兴说唱穿插其中。录制地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家前廊，背景音完全来自现场环境，包括蚊虫、飞机起降等真实声响，无任何后期音乐添加。专辑呈现了暴力对社区的全方位渗透，编辑选择采用创作者本人的简短评述替代传统乐评以呈现这一现实文献。收益将捐赠给致力于以公共卫生方法终结暴力的Cure Violence Global机构。

items.body: Berlin trio MNÆ issue their third single, “Drive”, on August 28, 2026, together with a video. The self-released track is the group’s first synthwave-leaning piece, and arrives four months after their debut. MNÆ bring an electronic body music and wave hybrid that mixes pulsing sequences, machine rhythms and pop hooks, and the band describe their sound as sitting “at the intersection of Wave, EBM, and modern electro”. “Drive” is the third instalment in a run that started in spring 2026. The trio released the single “Hold The Tide” on April 29, followed by the two-track “The Lion” on June 11, which paired the title track with an EvvilKing club edit of “Hold The Tide”. All three releases are self-released, written, mixed and mastered by the band. On “Drive” the group turn towards a period-conscious synthwave palette without reproducing it wholesale; the band describe the track as a modern interpretation of, and homage to, the pioneers of electro pop. MNÆ have not put “Drive” on Bandcamp ahead of release; the June single “The Lion” is the most recent release available there. The Lion by MNÆ About MNÆ MNÆ is an electronic trio formed in Berlin in 2026 by Arc Morten, Jan Wilking and Axel Tasler. All three arrived with a considerable amount of prior work behind them. Arc Morten sings and writes in Cyto, the Berlin duo he started with soundtrack composer Christoph Schauer in 2017 and which grew out of the Morphose circle. Jan Wilking and Axel Tasler have both been part of the German electro-industrial group Steril since its formation in Oldenburg in 1990, Wilking on keyboards and programming and Tasler on guitars and programming. Tasler also plays in Audiocall, whose recent records include “Know Your Murderer” in 2024, “A Different World” in 2025 and “Unintentional Presence – Part 2” in 2026. The EvvilKing alias, used for the club edit on “The Lion”, has appeared in the Steril camp since a remix credit on the 2002 single “I Get Closer”. The band opened its discography on April 29, 2026 with “Hold The Tide”, a self-released single written and produced by all three members. “The Lion” followed on June 11, 2026, adding a second original and the EvvilKing rework. Both are on Bandcamp, and the group’s YouTube channel carries videos for “The Lion” and for both versions of “Hold The Tide”. “Drive” continues that release run and pushes the project further towards melodic electro-pop while keeping the sequenced, club-facing base of the first two singles.
items._cn_summary: 柏林三人组MNÆ将于2026年8月28日发行第三支单曲《Drive》，这是他们首次明显倾向synthwave风格的作品。乐队自称定位在Wave、EBM与现代electro的交汇处，融合了脉冲式序列、机械节奏与流行hook。《Drive》被描述为对电子流行先驱者的现代诠释与致敬，既保持了前两支单曲的序列化和俱乐部化基底，又向旋律化电子流行方向推进。乐队成员均来自柏林电子场景的深厚背景：Arc Morten自2017年起经营双人项目Cyto，Jan Wilking与Axel Tasler则是1990年成立的德国电工业团体Steril的成员。文章详细梳理了乐队的发行时间线——从4月的首支单曲《Hold The Tide》到6月的《The Lion》双曲EP，再到即将到来的《Drive》——所有作品均为自主创作、混音与母带处理的独立发行。

items.body: Baltimore electro-industrial duo Pygmy Children released “Proof in Lies” on 21 August 2026 through Re:Mission Entertainment. The digital single carries two versions of the track, a short mix running 4:37 and a long mix running 6:42, and is the lead single from the brothers’ forthcoming fifth studio album “Into The Silence”. Pete Roper wrote the words and music. He and his brother Brian Roper produced and mixed the single, Jeff Mortimer mastered it, and Brian Roper made the cover art. The download is offered in MP3, FLAC and 24-bit/44.1 kHz. The song began with a notebook rather than a session. Pete Roper described the starting point as a set of lyrics he had abandoned years earlier: “I rediscovered some old lyrics in a notebook for a track that had never fully materialized. I still remembered the original chord progression, so I rewrote the lyrics, recorded the initial drum tracks, and the project began to take shape.” Proof in Lies by Pygmy Children How Pygmy Children built the ‘Proof in Lies’ video The accompanying video sets live performance footage against public-domain animation produced in the 1940s, recut by the duo and layered with original visual effects. Pete Roper set out what the assembled imagery is about: “The imagery in the video challenges our blurred perception of the boundary between reality and fantasy as we move through life increasingly disconnected from one another, following established paths without question and becoming desensitized to experiences beyond ourselves. The social acceptance of violence as a form of entertainment also emerges as a recurring theme. Finally, the unanswered question of what the recurring mysterious character possesses invites deeper interpretation.” No release date has been announced for “Into The Silence”. About Pygmy Children Pygmy Children are an electro-industrial duo from Baltimore, Maryland, made up of brothers Pete and Brian Roper. Pete Roper started on drums at fifteen and played in a speed metal band; Brian Roper began remixing that material on tape decks, and the project grew out of those experiments. The duo issued the “Face Down” EP in 1993 and the album “Malignant” in 1994 through No Name No Slogan, then signed to Cleopatra Records in 1995 for “Deconstruct”. A fourth release, “Low Life Dream”, followed in 1998 through the German label Out Of Line, with production input from George of Urania. Output stopped after that, and Pete Roper stated around 2005 that the project was over. The duo returned in 2025 by signing to Re:Mission Entertainment. The single “I Have No Name” arrived on 29 August 2025 with remixes by Frontal Boundary and Slipjoint, as announced when Pygmy Children return with new album ‘Coincidental Strategies’, first single out August 29. The five-track Pygmy Children release ‘Signal Unknown’ single/EP followed on 17 October 2025 with reworkings by Fermion, Interface, Deekay and George Hagegeorge. The album “Coincidental Strategies” arrived on 24 October 2025 as a digital release and a limited-edition CD, the duo’s first physical edition since 1998. They also played an East Coast run billed as the Resurrection Tour alongside Mentallo & The Fixer. Alongside their own catalogue the pair have taken on remix work for other Re:Mission Entertainment acts, including tracks on Frontal Boundary’s “Faith” EP and the album “Failure”. “Proof in Lies” is their first release of 2026 and opens the run-up to “Into The Silence”.
items._cn_summary: Pygmy Children 是来自巴尔的摩的兄弟二人组电工业组合，新单曲《Proof in Lies》是第五张专辑《Into The Silence》的首发曲目，包含短版与长版两个混音版本。创作源于主脑 Pete Roper 在旧笔记本中重新发现的早年废弃歌词，他将原有和弦进行保留，重新填词并录制初始鼓轨，使项目逐步成型。歌曲由 Roper 兄弟自行制作与混音，Jeff Mortimer 负责母带处理，提供 MP3、FLAC 与 24-bit/44.1 kHz 等多种数字格式。配套音乐影像以现场演出画面叠加 1940 年代公有领域动画素材，经组合再剪与自製视觉效果处理，探讨现实与幻想边界的模糊感、暴力的社会娱乐化等主题。该组合自 1993 年发表首张 EP 以来几经沉寂，2025 年签约 Re:Mission Entertainment 后回归。整体属于典型的工业电子范畴，与暗潮/工业偏好有交集，但在声音描述上缺乏实验性突破的细节。

items.body: Washington, D.C. darkwave duo 2DCAT released the four-track EP “We’re Here” on 21 August 2026 as a self-released digital edition, together with a video for the title track. The EP is credited to Johan Hauck and HAEZL, and downloads are offered in MP3, FLAC and 24-bit/44.1 kHz. The tracklist runs “We’re Here”, a Blue Rose edit of the 2024 single “Frames”, “Never Enough” and “Salvation Will Not Come”. No physical edition has been issued. We’re Here by 2DCAT Who is speaking on the 2DCAT track ‘We’re Here’ The title track is written from the point of view of the dead, addressing the living. Hauck was direct about how the lyric should be read, and about the reassurance in the chorus line “We’re here to remind you you’re never alone”: “We wouldn’t blame anyone for hearing this as hopeful. The gates being steeled, the door appearing, the path looking clear… that’s not hope. That’s dying. The dead are your guides because they’ve already made that walk.” HAEZL, an opera singer, delivers the vocal without theatrical menace. Hauck builds and fabricates the synthesizers heard on the track himself, and designs analogue instruments and FPGA-based hardware from scratch. The arrangement draws on early European synthpop and darkwave, with measured tempo and severe textures. The video keeps the frame near-black, with unstable light and coarse grain. “We’re Here” belongs to a run of recent singles pointing toward a next 2DCAT album, which has not yet been announced. About 2DCAT 2DCAT are a dark synthpop duo based in Washington, D.C., built around analogue synthesizers and drawing on synth music of the late 1970s and early 1980s. Johan Hauck handles synthesizers, drum machines and arrangements and has played in electro-industrial bands for around two decades. HAEZL sings and plays theremin, and has worked as a backing singer for The Beach Boys, Patti LaBelle, Cynthia Erivo, Renée Fleming and The Filharmonic, with television appearances on VH1, TLC and The Today Show. Guitarist Ulf has also appeared in the lineup. The project began releasing on Bandcamp in January 2019 with “Electric”, followed by “Summer, 1983” in April 2019 and “03:00” in September 2019. Three releases arrived in 2020: “Delaware is Burning” in February, “Modern Dystopia” in April and “Weeks Where Decades Happen” in November. “Fantastic Voyage” appeared in December 2022 and “Data Fusion” in September 2023. Seven releases followed in 2024: “The Darkest Hour” in March, “Love and Life (Part 2)” in April, “Falling Down” in May, “Take My Hand” in July, the set “Covers” in August, the single “Frames” in September and “Elegy” in November. “Covers” included a version of Allie X’s “Off With Her Tits”, reported at the time in 2DCAT cover Allie X track ‘Off With Her Tits’ – Out now. A remix collection followed in January 2025, “This is not for you.” in July 2025 and “Eat The Rich” in May 2026. Every release to date has come out without a label. The duo played their first German club dates in July 2026: Köln’s Club Volta on 24 July as part of the Echoes of Rebellion festival, Munich’s Theater Drehleier on 30 July and Leipzig’s Darkflower on 31 July. “We’re Here” is their first release since those shows.
items._cn_summary: 2DCAT是华盛顿特区的暗潮双人组合，核心成员Johan Hauck负责合成器与编曲，HAEZL担任主唱并演奏特雷门琴。Hauck自行设计模拟合成器与基于FPGA的硬件乐器，声响建立在自制器材之上，呈现出早期欧陆合成器流行与暗潮交织的质感。这张四曲EP以"亡者对生者说话"为概念，主打曲的歌词直指死亡而非希望，合唱线"我们在此提醒你永不孤单"被Hauck阐释为对临终通道的指引。HAEZL作为歌剧出身的歌手，以非戏剧化的方式呈现人声，与黑暗的合成器底色形成对照。视频画面压至极暗，配合不稳定光源与粗粝颗粒，强化了作品的主题氛围。整体制作倾向于模拟硬件与冷峻织体，属独立自发行的小众暗潮作品，在概念深度与声响自制上有一定追求，但在风格上仍属类型内的常规延伸。

items.body: On “Chouka”, Manal spends a whole song trying to talk a man into it, half in Darija, half in French, tossing him a “take it easy” one moment and a “sans politesse” the next. The flattery comes in brand names: he is a Tiffany diamond, a multivitamin in her blood, a car she floors down an endless highway. She is one of Morocco’s best-known pop singers, a rapper turned singer from Casablanca who made her name on songs about women and how society treats them. Lately she has thrown herself into raï, the working-class dance music of western Algeria and eastern Morocco, and said she wants to take it somewhere new. “Chouka” came out on 16 August, one of a run of singles Manal has fired out through 2026. items.body:
The Original Motion Picture Soundtrack for Crime 101 by experimental electronic musician, producer and composer Blanck Mass (She Rides Shotgun).

"Thunderous synth soundscapes are paired with nuanced character-driven themes creating a multi-faceted backdrop to the intense thriller. The Amazon MGM Studios film directed by Bart Layton is set against the sun-bleached grit of Los Angeles.

Crime 101 weaves the tale of an elusive jewel thief (Chris Hemsworth) whose string of heists along the 101 freeway have mystified police. When he eyes the score of a lifetime, his path crosses that of a disillusioned insurance broker (Halle Berry) who is facing her own crossroads. Convinced he has found a pattern, a relentless detective (Mark Ruffalo) is closing in, raising the stakes even higher. As the heist approaches, the line between hunter and hunted begins to blur, and all three are faced with life-defining choices– and the realization that there can be no turning back.

On creating the music, Power says :

“Crime 101 was an incredible movie to have the opportunity to score. At the centre of the story is, of course, the heist. However, it very quickly became apparent to me that this was not any heist movie, but more a Noir which happens to have a heist in it. The central characters and how their lives become intertwined was more important than the action, in a way. This is high-octane in parts, of course, but what really drew me to this movie was the character development. Lou, Davis and Sharon are the beating heart. I wanted to ‘be with them sonically’ throughout. Both the tender and the furious needed to be sympathetic with one another”."

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Blanck Mass为犯罪惊悚片《Crime 101》创作的原创电影配乐。作曲家以实验电子音乐人的身份切入，在轰鸣的合成器音景与细腻的角色主题之间建立对话，试图用声音伴随片中三位主角的命运交织。创作者明确表示影片虽有劫案元素，但本质是一部黑色电影，人物关系的张力高于动作场面，因此配乐需要在温柔与激烈之间找到共鸣，使两条情感线在声音层面彼此呼应。整体定位为高能量但以角色驱动的电子配乐，融合合成器质感与叙事张力。发行方为独立厂牌INVADA Records，属于当代电影配乐领域中带有实验色彩的跨界作品。

items.body:
Daria Lourd (Bored Lord) + her wife, vocalist Jaelynn Walls = DARLYNN on their debut shot of Jersey club meets ‘90s R&B, woozy garage house and vintage psych-funk flavours.

"Darlynn is an Oakland-based duo composed of Daria Lourd (aka Bored Lord) and her wife, vocalist Jaelynn Walls. Dyke Den is a lesbian love story about two creative individuals finding each other and themselves through effusive and contemplative sonic avenues. Created in their home over the course of two years, this album speaks to the journey of Daria and Jaelynn’s romantic relationship as well as their evolving combined creative impulses.

On Dyke Den, Darlynn display their influences – from Janet Jackson and Sly & the Family Stone, to Frankie Knuckles and Larry Levan – in a sophisticated, fully realized, and overtly queered fashion. Joyous dancefloor moments are abundant. Tracks like “Make Yr Move” and “Like A Summer” celebrate deep house vibes ala Alleviated Records, while sultry R&B moves are flexed on “Girl 2 Girl” and “Alright With Me.” But longing and yearning exist within this joyous arc, and the question arises: “How can I get you to love me?” More than an idealistic narrative of girl meets they/them, Dyke Den paints a portrait of love in all its multifaceted moments: the bids for commitment, the stagnation of years going by, the wormholes of desire. Yet the album maintains its thesis of hope. The sweet, layered harmonies of closing song “Love Letter” display the power of life partnership: “My whole life is a love letter to you.” Dyke Den features artwork by Hailee Va in a sleeve designed by Eloise Shir-Juen Leigh. Darlynn’s final declaration, “We are all creatures of desire, completely built for love.”s"
items._genre: jersey club / R&B / garage house / deep house / psych-funk
items._cn_summary: Darlynn由制作人Daria Lourd（Bored Lord）和人声Jaelynn Walls组成，这张处女作在两年间于家中完成，呈现出新泽西俱乐部节奏与九十年代R&B的交汇，并融合朦胧车库浩室与复古迷幻放克元素。专辑明确致敬Janet Jackson、Sly & the Family Stone、Frankie Knuckles和Larry Levan等前辈，曲目如《Make Yr Move》《Like A Summer》展现Alleviated Records式的深层浩室质感，《Girl 2 Girl》《Alright With Me》则呈现柔滑的R&B律动。整张作品不仅是音乐合集，更以两位女性的爱情历程为叙事主线——从吸引、渴望、承诺到岁月流逝中的倦怠，结尾曲《Love Letter》以层叠和声传达生活伴侣的亲密与希望。独立小厂牌发行，配有Eloise Shir-Juen Leigh设计的封面，整体在舞曲传统内完成了一次酷儿视角的深情表达。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Sticking together for one more album, Roger Sutton's Riff Raff pull off another very cool Jazz Rock album--something edging its way into the Canterbury conversation. Perhaps working in Kent (where Canterbury lies) with producer Ken Burgess (who would go on to work with Tommy Eyre's next band, Zzebra) had something to do with that.1. "Original Man" (7:40) this Peter Kirtley composition opens with a one minute whole band intro that borders on sounding like something from one of their Canterbury contemporaries, but then in the second minute things settle down into a very cool almost downtempo ambient electric lounge music over which Peter sings in a bit of a Dylanesque style. Peter's lead guitar play in the middle portends the coming of Stevie Ray Vaughan as well as paying a bit of an homage to his contemporary, Eric Clapton. What a great, powerful song to open an album with! Signs of good things to come! (14.375/15)2. "Havakak" (6:06) another really cool Jazz-Rock Fusion song that sounds like something National Health or The Soft Machine would have done. There is just such a great warmth to the feel of this palette and the soundscape it creates: no matter if the band is ripping through it (first motif), slowing things down (second motif), blues-rocking it (third motif), or vamping for Peter Kirtley's extended solo (fourth motif), the sound just wraps around you and makes you feel a part of it. And to think it was a composition that Peter brought from working with keyboard master Kenny Craddock and bassist Colin Gibson during their Mark-Almond days! (9.75/10)3. "Goddamm the Man" (6:09) a Roger Sutton original places us in a juke joint in the Louisiana/Mississippi swamp as raw steel-string acoustic guitars pick away Jack Johnson style from both the left and right while Roger's funky bass and Aureo's drums and congas and Tommy Eyre's stanky electric piano and organ add and increase the funky stink (everybody seems to have taken on at least two tracks). I didn't think I was going to like this once it opened (especially with Roger's Swamp-style American White Blues vocals) but once it got going, once the background vocals and horn section's accents were added, the funk just took over: I'm a fan! (9.25/10)4. "In the Deep" (3:59) Oh, my gosh! Is Robert Wyatt in the house? Peter Kirtley's second offering to the album finds us deep in the forlorn ballad forms that reluctantly came out of the Canterbury Scene. There is so much funky R&B in this--and it feels so solid and natural! Every nuance and subtlety injected, added, and feels so perfect, so genius, so easy! Shades of two of the best to ever do this style: Paddy McAloon (Prefab Sprout) and Roddy Frame (Aztec Camera) as well as the contemporary master extemporaneosifier, Richard Sinclair. Awesome and alarmingly good! (9.75/10)5. "The Waster" (5:09) feels a bit like a continuation or variation on a palette, pace, and style used in all of the previous songs (the sound French downtempo band AIR mastered for their massive hit, >). Roger Sutton's second composition finds him drifting more into the singing style of Eric Burdon (think "Drink This Wine"; even the lyrical format is very much like that iconic song). I love the laid-back vibe of the musicians' spacious note and chord play, a late night application of funk. Horn accents, smooth Fender Rhodes, congas and drums, background vocals, bluesy rhythm guitar, lead sax in the instrumental section, nice, easy-going two-chord construct (think Traffic's "Feelin' Alright"). It's nice, it's fun, it's warm, it's equally well performed as the album's previous material, just a little more tranquilizing. (8.875/10)6. "Tom's Song" (4:22) the title, of course, referring to keyboardist Tommy Eyre, who is the composer of this song. Though it starts out having a little trouble defining itself and its melodies for the first minute, it eventually metes out some quite lovely music: the piano playing and synth strings support quite lush and romantic. Roger's bass and Aureo's congas are muted into the background leaving the synth strings, piano, voice, and Steve Gregory's weirdly-effected flutes in the foreground. Tom's vocal is rather gentle, doubled up, I think. It's obviously a sad love song about regret. I like it's edgy classical and jazz influences as well as Tom's genuine emotion. (9/10)7. "Speed" (9:16) another great construct from multiple influences: the funky blues, American Southern Rock, Traffic, The Allman Brothers, and a little Van Morrison and The Doors in the mix. Another Roger Sutton original, I consider this to be not a particularly great or memorable "epic" but definitely another serious and high quality rendering. (17.625/20)Total Time 42:41It feels weird to be categorizing music coming from Great Britain with labels like "Southern Rock," "Swamp Rock" or "American Southern Rock" but they would not be the only British artists attracted to those types of American sounds. (Think of Alan Parker's film The Commitments and its characters' connection to the Memphis Horns and the music of Wilson Pickett.) Almost every British artist who was coming of age in the early 1960s would cite American Blues, Soul, R&B, and even Jazz as essential foundations and inspirations for their music. Roger Sutton, Peter Kirtley, Tommy Eyre, and Bud Beadle would be no different. I do, however, give the band credit for hearing and emulating a bit of their own countrymates of the Canterbury Style.A/five stars; an eclectic and full-blown masterpiece of sophisticated and highly-nuanced original music by some sadly-under-appreciated musicians (and band). HIGHLY recommended to any professed and self-respecting music lover.
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年的专辑由Riff Raff乐队录制，风格游走于爵士摇滚与坎特伯雷场景之间。Roger Sutton的贝斯与Tommy Eyre的键盘担当核心，Peter Kirtley的吉他在细腻弹拨与硬朗独奏间切换。专辑包含多种色彩：开场曲以乐队齐奏引入，渐入带有迪伦风格人声的电爵士氛围；中段曲目融合蓝调摇滚、放克节奏与路易斯安那沼泽意象，铜管点缀增添层次；翻唱作品保留了Mark-Almond时期Kenny Craddock与Colin Gibson合作时的温暖质感。人声演绎被作者拿来与Robert Wyatt、Richard Sinclair等人比较，体现出坎特伯雷特有的内敛情感表达。整体制作在Kent完成，由Ken Burgess操刀，音乐既有结构化编排，又保留即兴段落，是英国七十年代爵士摇滚场景中一张扎实但非突破性的作品。

items.body: Dwayne Goettel, keyboardist, sampling and programming specialist for the industrial band Skinny Puppy, died on 23 August 1995 at the age of 31. He was found dead at his parents’ home in Edmonton, Alberta, of an apparent heroin overdose. Thirty-one years on, Goettel remains one of the defining figures behind Skinny Puppy’s sound between 1986 and 1995. Dwayne Rudolph Goettel was born on 1 February 1964 in High Prairie, Alberta, Canada. A classically trained pianist, he grew up in Edmonton, where he played trumpet in his high school band before taking up piano and getting involved in the city’s small electronic music scene, including the groups Psyche and Water. He met cEvin Key in 1985 when Water opened for Skinny Puppy on their “Bites” tour. Key asked him to join the band the following year, replacing keyboardist Bill Leeb, who left to form Front Line Assembly. Goettel made his first contributions to Skinny Puppy on the album “Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse” (1986). His technical knowledge of samplers and studio equipment, particularly the Ensoniq Mirage, helped steer the band away from its early synth-pop sound toward the more abrasive, sample-driven style of “Cleanse Fold and Manipulate” (1987), “VIVIsectVI” (1988), “Rabies” (1989), “Too Dark Park” (1990) and “Last Rights” (1992). cEvin Key later credited Goettel’s early command of the technology, calling him “the master of sampling.” Alongside his work with Skinny Puppy, Goettel collaborated with Key on the side projects The Tear Garden, formed with singer Edward Ka-Spel, as well as Doubting Thomas, Hilt and Cyberaktif, which Key also shared with Bill Leeb. Goettel released solo material under the name aDuck and, in 1993, co-founded the label Subconscious Communications with Phil Western. Skinny Puppy’s eighth studio album, “The Process,” was recorded in Los Angeles beginning in 1993, but the sessions were marked by drug problems and conflict within the band. Vocalist Nivek Ogre quit in June 1995, and Goettel and Key returned to Vancouver with the master tapes. Goettel entered a rehabilitation programme in Edmonton before returning to work on Download, a side project he had started with Key. He was later readmitted to rehab. On 23 August 1995, Goettel was found dead at his parents’ home in Edmonton; his death was attributed to a heroin overdose. “The Process” was completed by Key and producer Dave “Rave” Ogilvie and released in 1996, dedicated to Goettel’s memory, as was Download’s debut album, “Furnace.” About Skinny Puppy Skinny Puppy formed in Vancouver, Canada, in 1982 as a side project for cEvin Key (born Kevin Crompton), who was also drumming in the new wave band Images in Vogue. Key recruited Nivek Ogre (Kevin Ogilvie) as vocalist, and the pair adopted stage names to avoid confusion between two members both named Kevin. The band self-released the EP “Back & Forth” in 1983 and signed to Vancouver label Nettwerk the same year. The EP “Remission” followed in December 1984, and Skinny Puppy’s debut full-length album, “Bites,” arrived in 1985. Bill Leeb, performing as Wilhelm Schroeder, joined on bass synth and backing vocals during this period. Leeb left the band in 1986 to form Front Line Assembly, and Dwayne Goettel replaced him, making his first contributions to “Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse” (1986). Skinny Puppy went on to release “Cleanse Fold and Manipulate” (1987), “VIVIsectVI” (1988) and “Rabies” (1989), the last featuring Ministry’s Al Jourgensen, followed by “Too Dark Park” (1990) and “Last Rights” (1992), the band’s final album for Nettwerk. In 1993 the group signed to Rick Rubin’s American Recordings and relocated to Los Angeles to record “The Process.” The sessions were affected by conflict and drug problems; Ogre quit in June 1995, and Goettel died two months later. Key and Dave “Rave” Ogilvie completed “The Process,” releasing it in 1996 in Goettel’s memory. Skinny Puppy reunited for a one-off performance at the Doomsday Festival in Dresden, Germany, in August 2000, leaving the keyboard station on stage empty in tribute to Goettel. The band reformed as a full-time project in 2003 with producer Mark Walk, releasing “The Greater Wrong of the Right” (2004), “Mythmaker” (2007), “HanDover” (2011) and “Weapon” (2013). In a 2023 interview, the band confirmed it had split up for good after more than four decades together. Goettel’s death on 23 August 1995 remains part of that history: 31 years on, his contribution to albums including “Too Dark Park” and “Last Rights” is remembered as central to Skinny Puppy’s sound.
items._cn_summary: 本文是对工业乐队Skinny Puppy成员Dwayne Goettel逝世31周年的纪念性回顾，详细梳理了其生平与音乐贡献。文章追溯了Goettel从古典钢琴出身、转投电子音乐场景的历程，重点描述了他如何凭借对Ensoniq Mirage采样器的精通，将Skinny Puppy从早期的合成器流行风格引导至更具攻击性的采样驱动型工业声响。文章涵盖了《Cleanse Fold and Manipulate》《VIVIsectVI》《Too Dark Park》等关键专辑的技术演变，以及The Tear Garden、Doubting Thomas等侧支项目的合作脉络。同时也记述了《The Process》录制期间乐队内部的毒品问题与冲突，最终以Goettel因海洛因过量去世的悲剧结尾，遗作由cEvin Key与制作人完成并发行。整体内容偏向人物传记与历史回顾，而非对具体音乐作品的深度乐评。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张芬兰手风琴与钢琴二重奏专辑，Kalaniemi与Alakotila合作长达三十五年，两人之间的默契通过无谱即兴得以充分展现。专辑收录多首传统曲目与原创作品，其中包括一首Piazzolla的探戈曲和一首芬兰式探戈，弦乐四重奏在标题曲中作为点睛之笔加入。整体风格平静而梦幻，乐器对话流畅而甜美，两位音乐家服务于旋律本身而非炫技，探索曲调的可能性。Kalaniemi的人声运用独特，既有无歌词哼唱也有歌词演唱。评论指出这不会撼动根基，却构成了纯粹而安静的聆听之美。作为世界音乐范畴的作品有一定文化特色，但缺乏实验性与跨界融合元素，整体风格偏向传统的民谣室内乐演奏。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: Dominique Cravic与地下漫画家Robert Crumb于1986年在巴黎相遇后组成了Les Primitifs du futur，这张专辑是他们的第五张录音。乐评以幽默口吻推测了他们的创作起源：在一堆78转唱片和阁楼中找到的乐器中拼贴出27首短曲。手风琴作为bal-musette传统的核心，贯穿全片，并与萨克斯、班卓琴、尤克里里、夏威夷吉他、锯琴、风笛等形成色彩斑斓的编制。曲目多为法语talk-sing演绎，风格混杂爵士乐、拉格泰姆、jug音乐、法国香颂与skiffle。亮点包括对1925年经典《Ukulele Lady》的重译，以及向2020年辞世的法国抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的《N'oublie pas Gréco》。乐评将其与同样难以归类的Dan Hicks & His Hot Licicks相提并论，强调老乐手们以严肃态度让被遗忘的曲调获得新生。Cravic所言"年轻人有火，我们有光"恰好概括了这张唱片的气质。
